The Fragrance of Tradition: Omani Rose Water from Al Jabal Al Akhdar

Have you ever wondered how a simple rose can carry hundreds of years of history, culture, and tradition?

The Journey of Rose Water

1
🏺✨

Then

People used traditional clay and stone furnaces (Al-Dahjan) along with copper pots for distillation.

Now

Modern distillation machines are used to make the production process easier and faster.

Why

Technology development and saving time/effort.

2
🏺✨

Then

Rose water was stored in traditional clay containers.

Now

Rose water is packaged in modern glass bottles.

Why

Modern methods help store and package rose water more conveniently and safely for quality.

3
🏺✨

Then

Rose water was mainly used for traditional home cooking, hospitality, and personal care.

Now

It is sold in local markets and to tourists, and is widely used in commercial perfumes, cosmetics, and other products.

Why

Increasing demand from tourists and economic development to create a source of income.

Discover the Traditions

Summary

Mountain rose water production is a traditional Omani custom which represents a deeply rooted agricultural heritage in Al Jabal Al Akhdar. In the past, local farmers harvested the fragrant petals in early spring and extracted the aromatic water manually using traditional clay ovens and primitive copper pots. However, the production process has changed over time as modern distillation equipment is now integrated. Despite these changes, it remains a vital cultural symbol.

Our response

In our view, we must actively preserve and protect this unique cultural heritage because it forms an irreplaceable pillar of our historical identity, traditional lifestyle, and local economy. Although expanding tourist markets and mass production have turned the industry far more commercialized than before, we believe that strictly supporting local farming families, regulating product quality, and maintaining original distillation standards will successfully keep the authentic craft alive for future generations to cherish and respect
